transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, well... I'm a bit embarrassed to even be here, honestly. I'm sure you deal with much more serious things. But I suppose what brings me in is... well, I've been noticing that I arrange quite a bit of my life—specifically my house—around, um, not seeing spiders. 

I know it sounds a bit silly for a grown woman, a teacher no less, but I just... I put off doing the laundry because it's down in the basement. And I've completely stopped going into the garden shed. I even—and this is the part I feel most foolish about—I even pay people to do small jobs around the house that I know perfectly well how to do myself, just because I can't quite make myself go into those spaces where they might be. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not wasting your time with this.
Is it just spiders that you're afraid of, or are there other creatures or objects that also cause you significant distress?

Oh, no, it's really just spiders. I'm perfectly fine with, you know, mice or bees or heights or anything else. It's just... them. 

And I know how silly it sounds, I really do. I tell my students to be rational, so I know perfectly well that a spider in the corner of an old house probably isn’t going to hurt me. I'm well aware of that. But... well, the moment I even picture one dropping out of a storage box, or just sitting there near the washer... it just feels enormous. And threatening, in a way I’m honestly so embarrassed to admit to a professional like yourself. 

I hope that doesn't sound too ridiculous? I just can't seem to logic my way out of that feeling, if that makes sense.
Have you ever attempted to confront or be in a situation where you knew there would be spiders, or do you always try to avoid such situations?

Well, um... I really do try to be brave, I promise. But to be completely honest, I almost always just avoid them. 

I suppose that's exactly what I meant earlier when I said I keep arranging my whole routine around not seeing them. I really wish I could just confront it like a normal person, but... well, like I mentioned, I just end up putting off the laundry for days because the machines are down in the basement. And the garden shed is just completely off-limits to me now. I just can't make myself go into those spaces if I think there's even a chance one might be there. 

I'd really just rather pay someone else to do those little jobs I know perfectly well how to do myself, just to be safe. I know it's terrible, and I know I should try harder to face it... I hope that answers your question alright?
Have you ever avoided going to a place or event because you thought there might be spiders there?

Well, yes... I suppose I have. I mean, I try not to let it ruin my life or anything dramatic like that. I'm a responsible person. But... yes. 

It's mostly just around my own home, really. Like I was saying before, I just... I avoid the basement where the laundry is, and I don't go into the garden shed anymore. And I feel awful even saying this again because it sounds so lazy, but I really do end up paying handymen to fix little things in those areas, just so I don't have to go in there. 

I don't usually cancel plans with friends or anything like that, if that's what you mean. I try very hard not to be an inconvenience to anyone else. It's really just my own spaces that I arrange around... well, avoiding them. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm explaining this properly.
Have you ever felt that your fear of spiders has interfered with your daily life or relationships in a significant way?

Well, I... I wouldn't say it's ruined any relationships or anything like that. I'm very careful to keep it from affecting my friends or my students. I always try to handle it quietly on my own. 

But I suppose... well, if I'm being completely honest, it has made things a bit difficult around the house. It's just... owning this place has gotten a little harder to manage, and honestly, more expensive than it should be. Because I let the laundry back up, and I can't go into the shed or the basement... I end up paying people for all this small maintenance help that I really should just be doing myself. 

I feel so silly admitting that to you. I know I should just put on some boots and go down there and deal with it like a responsible adult. But it's just so hard to force myself into those parts of the property I need to use. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely incompetent? I really do try to keep everything else in my life running smoothly... I just struggle with this one little area. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had to change your daily routine in a significant way because of your fear of spiders?

Well, um... I wouldn't call it a *significant* change, exactly. I still go to work every day, and I grade my students' papers on time, I promise. I really try to keep things as normal as possible. 

But, I suppose... like I was mentioning just a moment ago, it has changed how I do things around my own home. It's just... owning this house has become a lot more expensive and, well, harder to manage than I ever thought it would be. Because I'm paying for all this small maintenance help, and letting chores like the laundry back up, and just completely avoiding parts of the property I really need to use... 

I know it sounds terrible, and I know I'm repeating myself, I'm sorry. I just... I wish I didn't have to arrange my whole home life around this. I hope I'm not coming across as too much of a mess? I really am very organized at school, I promise. I just... I struggle with this at home. Is that the kind of routine change you meant?
Have you ever avoided social gatherings or events at someone else's home because you thought there might be spiders there?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. Like I touched on a little bit earlier, I really try my hardest not to let this affect my friends or colleagues. I would never want to offend a host or seem antisocial by turning down an invitation over... well, over my own silly issues. 

If I'm invited to a dinner party or a gathering at someone else's home, I always make sure to go. I'd be absolutely mortified if anyone thought I was being rude or difficult. I suppose if I ever felt nervous there, I would just put on a brave face and keep it to myself. I really do pride myself on being a good, reliable friend. So, no, I haven't avoided any social events like that. I hope that's a good sign? I really do try to handle myself properly when I'm around other people.
Have you ever turned down a job or career opportunity because it might involve being in situations where you could encounter spiders?

Oh, no, I would never do that. I've been a secondary school teacher for a long time, and I take my career very seriously. I would never let something like this get in the way of my professional responsibilities. 

I mean, I suppose if a position involved... I don't know, working out in the woods or cleaning out old barns, I might think twice, but that's not really in my field anyway. As a teacher, I'm mostly in the classroom or the staff room, and those are kept very clean and tidy. 

I've always been very dependable at work. I've never turned down a role or an extra assignment because of... well, because of my fear. I always want my principal and my colleagues to know they can count on me. I hope that shows that I'm still functioning well professionally? I really do try my best to be a good employee.
How would you describe the level of anxiety or fear you feel when you think about or encounter spiders?

Well, um... I try very hard to be rational about it, I really do. I'm a practical person, and I know a spider in the corner of an old house probably isn't going to hurt me. I always tell myself that they're more scared of us than we are of them, just like they say. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, it's... well, it's a bit overwhelming. The moment I just picture one dropping out of a storage box, or sitting there near the washer when I'm trying to do laundry... it suddenly feels enormous. And deeply threatening, in a way I'm really quite embarrassed to admit. 

I know it sounds so silly for a grown woman to be this frightened of a tiny bug. I really try not to let my imagination run away with me like that. I hope you don't think I'm being too ridiculous? I know I should be able to just brush it off.

Would you say that your fear of spiders is something that you are aware of and can acknowledge, but doesn't completely control your actions, or is it so intense that it significantly dictates what you do and don't do on a daily basis?

Well, um... I really do try to not let it control me, especially around other people, like I said. I want to be sensible about it. But... I suppose, if I'm being perfectly honest about how things are at home... it might dictate a bit more than I'd like to admit. 

I've sort of realized lately that I've been arranging my own house around... well, around not seeing them. It's so embarrassing to say out loud, but I'll put off doing the laundry for days because the machines are down in the unfinished part of the basement. And I just completely avoid the garden shed now. I even... oh, this is so silly... I even pay people to do small maintenance jobs around the house that I know perfectly well how to do myself, just because I can't make myself go into those dark little spaces where they might be. 

I know it's completely irrational to let it affect my daily chores like that. I really am trying to do better, I promise. I just... I couldn't keep living around it like that, which is why I decided I needed to come see you. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm completely helpless.
Have you ever felt like your fear of spiders has prevented you from doing something you wanted or needed to do at home?

Well, um... I suppose I did just mention the laundry and the shed, didn't I? I really hope I'm not making it sound like my house is falling apart or anything. I do keep the main living areas very tidy, I promise. 

But... yes, I suppose it has gotten a bit out of hand recently. I mean, owning this house... it's just become so much more expensive and difficult to manage than it should be. Like I said, I'm paying handymen for these tiny little maintenance jobs—things I know I could easily fix myself if I just... if I could just make myself go into the crawlspace or behind the water heater. And letting the chores back up, avoiding whole parts of my own property that I really need to use... 

I know it's not very sensible of me. A homeowner should be able to take care of her own house, shouldn't she? I feel quite ashamed that I've let it get to this point, where it's actually costing me money and making my home life harder. I really am trying to be more responsible about it, though. I hope you can see that I'm taking the right steps by being here?
Have you ever felt like your fear of spiders has caused you significant distress or impairment in your daily life?

Well, um... I guess I sort of already admitted to that, didn't I? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly. 

But yes, I suppose it really has become quite an impairment, if I'm being honest. Owning this house... it really has become so much more expensive and, well, harder to manage than it ever should be for someone my age. Like I was saying, I'm paying for help with all these small maintenance things, and I'm letting my chores back up, and just completely avoiding parts of the property that I really do need to use. 

I know it sounds terrible when I put it all together like that. I really don't want you to think I'm completely incapable of taking care of myself or my home. I am a very responsible person in every other area of my life, I truly am. It's just this one silly thing that's gotten so out of hand. I'm doing the right thing by trying to fix it now, aren't I?
Have you ever felt like your fear of spiders has led you to avoid activities that are important to you?

Oh, my... I feel terrible, I think I might be giving you the exact same examples all over again. I hope I'm being a good patient and answering these right? I really do want to be helpful. 

But, yes, taking care of my home is very important to me. I've always taken a lot of pride in being self-sufficient. So... like I was just saying a moment ago, avoiding those parts of the property I really need to use—like the shed or the basement—it stops me from doing the everyday upkeep and the gardening I normally enjoy. It just makes managing the whole house so much harder, and certainly more expensive, since I have to keep paying for outside help for those small maintenance things instead of just doing them myself. 

I do feel quite silly repeating myself, I'm so sorry. I really do try to keep the main parts of the house looking lovely, though. I hope you can see that I am trying my best to handle things properly. Is that the sort of activity you meant?
Have you ever felt like your fear of spiders has led you to avoid activities that you previously enjoyed?

Oh, dear... I feel like a broken record, I really do. I hope you're not getting frustrated with me for bringing up the same things again. Am I doing this right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

But, well... yes. I used to love gardening, for instance. I took such pride in my flowerbeds. But now, keeping up with the yard work means going into the shed for the tools, or clearing out the brush where... where they might be. So I've just been avoiding it. 

It's like I was saying before, owning this house has just become so much harder to manage. I'm letting those outdoor chores back up, and I'm paying people to do the weeding and the little maintenance things outside that I used to actually enjoy doing myself. I'm just avoiding whole areas of my own property that I used to spend hours in. 

I know it sounds like I've just let everything go, but I promise the inside of the house is still very well-kept. I just... I really want to get back to being the kind of person who enjoys her garden. I'm hoping this is the right way to start fixing things?
Have you ever felt like your fear of spiders has prevented you from doing something you wanted or needed to do outside of your home?

Oh, outside of the home... um... I'm trying to think. I really want to give you a good example, I know you need all the details to help me. 

But honestly, I don't think it really affects me much when I'm out and about. It's mostly just... just around my own house and yard, where I know the dark corners are. When I'm at school teaching, or running errands, or visiting friends, I don't really think about it. I mean, I suppose if I saw one at the grocery store I might be startled, but I haven't really avoided going anywhere outside my property because of it. 

I'm sorry, I hope that's an okay answer? I know it's not a very exciting one. I just haven't noticed it stopping me from doing things away from home. Is that normal, for it to just be tied to my own house?
Have you ever felt like your fear of spiders has prevented you from doing something you wanted or needed to do in your daily routine outside of household chores?

Oh, um... let me think. I really want to give you a helpful answer. But... outside of the household chores and the gardening... no, I don't believe so. 

My daily routine is mostly just going to the high school to teach, and maybe running an errand or two on the way home. I'm very diligent about my schedule, actually. I would never let something like this interfere with my students or my job. I try very hard to be professional and keep everything running smoothly. So, no, it really hasn't prevented me from doing those normal, everyday things in my routine. 

I feel a bit bad that I keep saying no to these questions about things outside of my chores! I hope I'm not making your job harder by not having more examples for you. Is it alright that my routine is mostly unaffected, as long as I just avoid those trouble spots at home?
Would you say that your fear of spiders has caused you to avoid certain activities or situations almost all the time?

Well, yes, I suppose that's exactly it. I... I hope I'm explaining this clearly, I know I keep circling back to the house. But that's really what brings me in here today. 

I just realized that I'm constantly arranging my own home life around not seeing them. Like I mentioned with the gardening... but it's also inside. I put off doing the laundry because the machines are down in the unfinished part of the basement. I completely avoid the garden shed. And, like I said, I'm paying people to do these small, silly little jobs around the property that I know perfectly well how to do myself. I just... I can't make myself go into those spaces where I know they might be. 

It sounds so silly when I say it out loud, a grown woman avoiding her own basement. I'm a bit embarrassed to admit how much I've let it dictate my chores. I really try to be capable and independent. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of picture of what's going on.
Has your fear of spiders ever caused you significant distress or impairment in your relationships with friends, family, or at work?

Um... no, not with my friends or family, I don't think. And definitely not at work. I pride myself on being very professional at the high school, so I always make sure to keep those things separate. I hope that's okay, that it doesn't really affect my social life or my job? 

But... as far as distress or impairment goes... well, I guess it really just comes back to the house. I'm a little embarrassed to admit this part, actually. But owning this home has become... well, it's become quite a bit more expensive and just harder to manage overall. 

Because I'm... I'm paying for small maintenance help for things I am perfectly capable of doing myself. And I'm letting my regular chores back up, and just completely avoiding parts of the property that I really need to use. It feels terrible to be wasting money and falling behind like that, because I really do try to be a responsible, organized person. I just can't bring myself to go into those spaces. Does... does that count as the kind of impairment you're looking for? I hope I'm answering your questions correctly.
Does your fear of spiders only occur when you are at home, or have you experienced it in other locations as well?

Um... no, I really think it's mostly just at home. I hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, constantly bringing it back to my house! I really do want to give you the most helpful answers I can. 

But... well, when I'm at the high school, or out running errands, it honestly doesn't even cross my mind. I suppose those places are just so public and well-kept that I don't feel the need to worry about them being there. So it really is just my own basement and my garden shed that cause me all this trouble. 

Is... is it normal for it to be so localized like that? I hope it's okay that I don't have examples from other places. I just wouldn't want you to think I'm being overly dramatic about my own home, it's just the only place it really seems to happen.
